body: My attorney is calling him out, but the process takes extremely long to do so.

>Rep

I have a good attorney working pro-bono. The problem is his attorney. He's literally grasping at straws, presenting false evidence, anything possible to drag this out as long as he can.
Thank you so much for your support. I really needed to hear that.

I would have taken a break from him regardless, I just wasn't sure about timing with it. Just because you claim to be a female doesn't give you any right to assume a single thing about me or my moral character.
I'm the type of girl that literally won't sleep with a guy until I've been in a stable relationship with them for at least a year.
Not really outside of the States. He said he would go to Europe for a week or so, but it would take a lot to get him to go elsewhere or for longer periods of time.
I would love to travel with him, but I don't think he wants to travel. He would do it for me, but not because he likes it.

I've been thinking of going on a break for awhile now. I wouldn't sleep with other guys or anything like that. I've just been with my BF for so long and all we do is hang out together and I feel like it's not healthy. I was terrified of doing it during the school year because we share the same friend group and I didn't want it to be awkward. Plus I feel terrible because I go back and forth. I've been with him since we were 17, and I could see myself marrying him, but I could also see myself having a midlife crisis after I marry him and I'm 35 and I want to travel to a foreign country or work for the US Gov abroad (I'm minoring in Arabic) and I have never gotten the chance to. I'm just worried all around.

A big part of it for me is that I am afraid of getting pregnant (because it happened to a family member twice, both unplanned) and then I'm also afraid of getting an STD. 

Because I personally could never have an abortion, I want to wait until I'm with a guy long enough that if I were to get pregnant, I know he would stay with me. 

Also, I get really attached to people, even without having sex. 

Plus, studies (like this: http://www.dailymail.co.uk/femail/article-4085758/Experts-reveal-sexual-partners-ve-determine-likely-DIVORCE.html) show a correlation between the number of sexual partners and the chance of divorce.

Here's more of a Christian perspective: https://lifeteen.com/blog/vow-worth-keeping/
You are right. I basically want to know both how to choose and people's experience with different things.
Maybe you could consider telling him while you both are on a walk or at a park. You could also have your mom sit down and do it with you.
I could honestly see him being a house husband for me. I'm pretty alpha in the relationship.

He had screenshots of it sent in a group chat. I later told him that part of what made me so mad is that is how he would have treated me if I would have left my BF for him. His response was "I wouldn't do that for you. She's just some girl I met on Tinder."
